title: Slovenia Caught Between Fiscal Strain and Foreign-Policy Controversy · 03 Sep
keywords: Slovenia, economy, inflation, fiscal deficit, EU fiscal rules, Israel, Palestine, foreign policy, persona non grata, RTV Slovenija, Eurovision, Robert Golob, European Commission, Bank of Slovenia, Gaza
notes: Slovenia is grappling simultaneously with an economy that has yet to fully normalize after years of inflationary pressure and a foreign policy stance on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict that is drawing both admiration and sharp criticism at home and in Brussels. With the government's deficit edging toward the EU's 3% ceiling and two Israeli ministers declared persona non grata in an unprecedented move, Ljubljana finds itself navigating unusually turbulent waters. The twin pressures are testing public patience and raising questions about the government's priorities.
